product.name: [Product] Remote Monitoring & Support for pump/valve controller
product.versions: Controller FW x.y · Gateway FW x.y · Cloud release YYYY.MM · App x.y
product.intendedPurpose: Remote monitoring of wastewater pump stations and valve controllers (levels, flows, pump states, alarms) and remote support / parameter changes by authorised manufacturer and customer technicians.
product.foreseeableUse: Operation at unmanned sites; use on flat OT networks without segmentation; shared technician accounts; remote access left permanently enabled; connection via customer-supplied routers; use beyond end of support.
product.users: Utility operator (read, acknowledge alarms) · Customer technician (setpoints) · Manufacturer support (remote session) · Integrator (commissioning)
product.environment: Wastewater utilities (NIS2 Annex I essential sector); unattended outdoor pump stations; LTE or customer Ethernet uplink; public cloud backend operated by manufacturer.
product.essentialFunctions: Local pump/valve control MUST continue without connectivity; alarm delivery; local manual override.
product.rdps: Cloud backend, support portal, device management service
product.outOfScope: Customer SCADA, customer network, technician laptops (assumptions recorded in Zones sheet)
product.personalData: Operator names, phone numbers / e-mails for alarm notification; technician IDs in logs

risks.scenario: Stolen or phished technician credentials used to open a remote session and change pump setpoints / disable pumps.
risks.consequence: Overflow at one or more stations; environmental incident
risks.controls: Phishing-resistant MFA (FIDO2) for all support accounts; named per-technician accounts, no shared logins; RBAC separating monitor-only and write roles; write sessions require operator approval; anomaly alerting on logins.
risks.evidence: Pen-test report §x; IdP config export; RBAC matrix

risks.scenario: Remote-access tunnel is permanently available, allowing access without the site operator's knowledge.
risks.controls: Remote write access disabled by default; sessions operator-initiated or approved, time-limited (e.g. 2 h) and auto-terminated; local physical kill switch / HMI toggle; visible session indicator on HMI.
risks.evidence: Default config checklist; test case TC-RS-01..05

risks.scenario: Compromise of cloud backend used to send commands to all connected sites (fleet-wide attack).
risks.controls: Gateway enforces command allowlist and value ranges locally; safety limits in controller not writable remotely; tenant isolation; signed commands; cloud admin MFA + PAM; no inbound ports on gateway.
risks.evidence: Architecture review; cloud pen-test; ISO 27001 SoA

risks.scenario: Man-in-the-middle on gateway–cloud link to read or alter telemetry and commands.
risks.controls: Mutual TLS 1.3 with per-device certificates; key stored in secure element; certificate pinning to manufacturer CA; certificate revocation.
risks.evidence: TLS config scan; key provisioning procedure

risks.scenario: Malicious or tampered firmware delivered through the update channel.
risks.controls: Code-signing with key in HSM; signature verification + secure boot on gateway; anti-rollback; reproducible / audited build pipeline.
risks.evidence: Secure boot test; HSM key ceremony record

risks.scenario: Actions in remote sessions cannot be attributed or reconstructed after an incident.
risks.controls: Per-user session logging of every parameter change (old/new value, user, time, site); tamper-protected log storage; logs exportable to customer SIEM.

risks.scenario: Denial of service on gateway or cloud prevents alarm delivery during a high-water event.
risks.controls: Controller keeps local autonomous control; local horn/SMS fallback alarm; cloud rate limiting & DDoS protection; connectivity-loss alarm.

risks.scenario: Known exploitable vulnerability in third-party component (e.g. OpenSSL, BusyBox, Linux kernel) on the gateway.
risks.controls: SBOM per release; continuous vulnerability monitoring; patch SLA by severity; no known exploitable vulns at release (release gate).

risks.scenario: On-site service port used to bypass cloud authentication and modify configuration.
risks.controls: Service port disabled by default, enabled per session; local unique credentials; physical seal / tamper indication; all local changes logged & synced.

risks.scenario: Default or shared password on gateway web UI used to gain administrative access.
risks.controls: Unique per-device credentials or forced change at commissioning (no skip option – see EN 18031 OJ restriction); brute-force lockout; web UI not exposed on WAN.

P1-2b.implementation: Remote write access and service port off by default; unique per-device credentials; factory reset via HMI.

P1-2g.implementation: Only process telemetry and alarm-routing contacts collected; no location tracking of technicians.

P2-5.implementation: CVD policy published at /security; triage SLA 5 working days.
